summary: According to the DGHS, the total death toll from dengue has now reached 458, with cumulative cases at 147,580 this year. Over 5,800 patients are currently undergoing treatment nationwide.

Bangladesh reports 3 more dengue deaths and 1,674 new hospitalisations in 24 hours. The total death toll this year has climbed to 458.

At least three dengue patients died and 1,674 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours till 8:00am yesterday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The cumulative number of dengue cases across the country has now reached 147,580. Currently, 5,826 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at various hospitals nationwide.

headline_marked: [[Second bus set ablaze in Dhaka]] in a single night, raising security concerns
headline: Second bus set ablaze in Dhaka in a single night, raising security concerns
summary: A Shohag Paribahan bus caught fire at Mohakhali terminal shortly before 1 AM Sunday, following another arson attack on a Bihanga Paribahan bus in Mirpur hours earlier. This marks two bus fires in the capital within a single night.
details: A Shohag Paribahan bus was set on fire at Dhaka's Mohakhali bus terminal shortly before 1 AM on Sunday, marking the second such incident in the capital within a single night. Two units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence were dispatched to the scene.
Shahjahan Hossain, an officer at the Fire Service control room, confirmed they received the report at 12:57 AM. Units from Tejgaon Fire Station promptly responded to the incident.

Hours earlier, around 10 PM on Saturday, a Bihanga Paribahan bus was deliberately set on fire in Mirpur. Police reported that individuals on a motorcycle poured petrol through a window onto the rear section of the parked bus before igniting it.

Although the bus staff managed to extinguish the flames, several seats in the back of the Bihanga Paribahan bus sustained damage. These incidents have reportedly raised security alarms in the capital.
